---
title: "Stream a matrix in Python"
description: "Process a matrix chunk by chunk with `open_stream`, and read only the cells you select."
jupyter: python3
---

```{python}
#| include: false
# scripts/render_docs.sh copies tests/fixtures/tiny into SCX_DOCS_WORK.
import os

os.chdir(os.environ["SCX_DOCS_WORK"])
```

`picklerick.open_stream` hands you the count matrix as a sequence of CSR row
blocks instead of one object in memory. Decoding runs on a background thread
a few chunks ahead of your loop, so peak memory is set by the chunk size,
not the file. This page is Python-only; the R package reaches the same
engine through `PicklerickMatrix()`, a DelayedArray backend.

The example file, `tiny.h5ad`, has 6 cells and 5 genes. A chunk size of 2 is
used so that the loop has several chunks to show; the default is 5000.

## Chunks

Each chunk is a `MatrixChunk`: NumPy arrays for the CSR row pointer, column
indices and values, plus `row_offset`, the position of its first row in the
full matrix.

```{python}
import picklerick as pk

for chunk in pk.open_stream("tiny.h5ad", chunk_size=2):
    print(chunk.row_offset, chunk.nrows, chunk.dtype, chunk.indptr.tolist())
```

## Per-cell totals without loading the matrix

`chunk.to_scipy()` wraps a chunk as a `scipy.sparse.csr_array` that shares
its arrays, so any sparse operation works on it. Here the totals per cell are
filled in chunk by chunk; `inspect(..., names=True)` gives the cell names
without opening the file with anndata.

```{python}
import numpy as np

info = pk.inspect("tiny.h5ad", names=True)
totals = np.zeros(info["n_obs"])
for chunk in pk.open_stream("tiny.h5ad", chunk_size=2):
    rows = slice(chunk.row_offset, chunk.row_offset + chunk.nrows)
    totals[rows] = chunk.to_scipy().sum(axis=1)

dict(zip(info["obs_names"], totals.tolist()))
```

The same totals from the whole matrix in memory:

```{python}
import anndata as ad

adata = ad.read_h5ad("tiny.h5ad")
np.allclose(totals, np.asarray(adata.X.sum(axis=1)).ravel())
```

## Filtering genes in one pass

A per-gene statistic needs every cell, but not all of them at once: add each
chunk's contribution as it streams by. Counting the cells in which each gene
is nonzero gives the usual "detected in at least one cell" filter, which is
what `rowSums(counts(sce) > 0) > 0` computes on a lazy matrix in R. Stored
zeros are left out with `chunk.data != 0`.

```{python}
n_cells = np.zeros(info["n_vars"], dtype=np.int64)
for chunk in pk.open_stream("tiny.h5ad", chunk_size=2):
    n_cells += np.bincount(chunk.indices[chunk.data != 0], minlength=info["n_vars"])

keep = n_cells > 0
dict(zip(info["var_names"], n_cells.tolist()))
```

The same counts from the matrix in memory:

```{python}
np.array_equal(n_cells, np.asarray((adata.X > 0).sum(axis=0)).ravel())
```

`keep` can then select genes wherever they are used, e.g.
`adata[:, keep]` once the data does fit, or the `var` mask of a later write.

## Reading only some cells

`where` selects cells by their `obs` values and `rows` by position. On h5ad
and Zarr files only the selected rows are read from disk, so a filter costs
what the matching cells cost. A chunk never spans a gap in the selection, and
`row_offset` still refers to the full matrix.

```{python}
for chunk in pk.open_stream("tiny.h5ad", where={"cell_type": "T"}):
    print(chunk.row_offset, chunk.nrows)

np.flatnonzero(adata.obs["cell_type"] == "T").tolist()
```

```{python}
for chunk in pk.open_stream("tiny.h5ad", rows=[0, 1, 4]):
    print(chunk.row_offset, chunk.nrows)
```

## Streaming by gene

Some work goes gene by gene over every cell: one model per gene, or
per-gene statistics too wide to accumulate. Rows of a cell-major matrix hold
genes scattered across every chunk, so for this the matrix is first written
stored by gene (CSC). `convert(..., gene_major=True)` does that, in a bounded
memory budget (`transpose_mem`, in GB); anndata reads the result as a
`csc_matrix`.

```{python}
pk.convert("tiny.h5ad", "tiny_by_gene.h5ad", gene_major=True)
pk.inspect("tiny_by_gene.h5ad")["x_axis"]
```

`open_stream(..., axis="var")` then hands out blocks of whole genes. Each
chunk's `to_scipy()` is a `csc_array` of every cell by the block's genes, and
`var_offset` is its first gene.

```{python}
for chunk in pk.open_stream("tiny_by_gene.h5ad", axis="var", chunk_size=2):
    Y = chunk.to_scipy()
    means = np.asarray(Y.mean(axis=0), dtype=float).ravel()
    print(chunk.var_offset, chunk.ncols, Y.shape, means.round(2).tolist())
```

`genes` selects genes the way `rows` selects cells, as `(start, stop)` ranges
or indices, so independent jobs can each take a slice of the genes:

```{python}
[(c.var_offset, c.ncols) for c in pk.open_stream("tiny_by_gene.h5ad", axis="var", genes=[(3, 5)])]
```

See [`open_stream`](../reference/python/open_stream.qmd) for every option.
